quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: When the accounting firm switched from hourly billing to fixed monthly fees for its regular clients, several senior accountants worried that revenue would fall. Instead, client retention improved noticeably, and two long-time clients who had been considering other firms renewed multi-year contracts within the first quarter of the new pricing model.
options: Client retention worsened after the pricing model changed.
The new pricing model appears to have strengthened client loyalty.
Every client left the firm after the change.
Fixed pricing always causes clients to leave immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The new pricing model appears to have strengthened client loyalty.
quests.hint: Notice what happened to client retention, not just revenue, after the change.
quests.explanation: Retention improved and clients renewed long-term contracts after the switch to fixed pricing, suggesting the new model made clients more likely to stay.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city museum that once displayed only paintings from its home country began rotating in works borrowed from museums abroad. Visitor numbers from outside the immediate region grew steadily over the following two years, and gift shop sales of exhibition catalogs nearly doubled.
options: Visitor numbers fell once the museum added international works.
The museum stopped displaying any paintings from its home country.
The international rotations seem to have broadened the museum's audience.
Every visitor to the museum comes from outside the region.
quests.correctAnswer: The international rotations seem to have broadened the museum's audience.
quests.hint: Think about who might be newly drawn to the museum by works from abroad.
quests.explanation: Visitors from outside the region increased after international works were added, suggesting the broader collection attracted people who might not have visited otherwise.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional hospital network required all new hires in its emergency department to complete an extra week of simulation-based training before working unsupervised. Two years later, the network reported a measurable decline in reported medication errors during night shifts specifically, though day-shift error rates stayed roughly the same.
options: Medication errors increased across every shift after the training began.
The extra training may have had its clearest effect on night-shift performance.
Day-shift error rates dropped more than night-shift rates.
The extra training had no measurable effect on any shift.
quests.correctAnswer: The extra training may have had its clearest effect on night-shift performance.
quests.hint: Notice which specific shift showed a change in error rates.
quests.explanation: Night-shift medication errors declined after the extra training was introduced, while day-shift rates barely changed, suggesting the training's benefit showed up most clearly at night.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A navigation app updated its algorithm to avoid routing drivers through residential neighborhoods whenever a comparable route using major roads was available. Several city councils that had previously received complaints about cut-through traffic reported a drop in resident complaints within months of the update.
options: Resident complaints increased after the app's update.
The app began routing drivers through neighborhoods more often.
City councils never received complaints about traffic before the update.
The app's routing change appears to have reduced cut-through traffic complaints.
quests.correctAnswer: The app's routing change appears to have reduced cut-through traffic complaints.
quests.hint: Compare complaint levels before and after the app changed its routing.
quests.explanation: Complaints about cut-through traffic dropped after the navigation app began avoiding residential routes, suggesting the update addressed a problem residents had raised.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Although his job requires him to travel almost every week, Deepak insists on video-calling his children every single night at their bedtime, no matter which time zone he happens to be in.
options: Deepak rarely contacts his children while traveling.
Deepak's job does not require any travel.
Deepak makes a consistent effort to stay connected with his children despite his travel.
Deepak's children refuse to speak with him during his trips.
quests.correctAnswer: Deepak makes a consistent effort to stay connected with his children despite his travel.
quests.hint: Think about what calling every night, regardless of time zone, shows about Deepak's priorities.
quests.explanation: Calling his children every night despite frequent travel and changing time zones shows that Deepak works hard to stay connected with them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A furniture retailer noticed that customers who used its augmented-reality app to preview a couch in their own living room before buying returned the item at less than half the rate of customers who ordered based on photos alone.
options: Previewing furniture with augmented reality seems to reduce returns.
The augmented-reality app increased the rate of returns.
Return rates were identical regardless of how customers shopped.
Customers who used the app always kept every item they bought.
quests.correctAnswer: Previewing furniture with augmented reality seems to reduce returns.
quests.hint: Compare the return rates between the two groups of customers.
quests.explanation: Customers who previewed furniture using the app returned items far less often than those who relied on photos, suggesting the preview helped set more accurate expectations.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Researchers monitoring a coastal wetland found that the area restored with native grasses supported nearly three times as many bird species as a nearby section restored with a single fast-growing non-native grass, even though both areas received identical amounts of rainfall and sunlight.
options: The non-native grass section supported more bird species overall.
Rainfall and sunlight were the main factors affecting bird diversity.
Both restored sections attracted the exact same number of bird species.
Using native grasses appears more effective at supporting bird diversity than non-native grasses.
quests.correctAnswer: Using native grasses appears more effective at supporting bird diversity than non-native grasses.
quests.hint: Compare the bird diversity in each section, and note what factors were held equal.
quests.explanation: The native-grass section supported far more bird species despite identical rainfall and sunlight, suggesting the type of vegetation, not the weather, made the difference.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A district that switched from grading homework for accuracy to grading it only for completion saw students report less anxiety about schoolwork in a year-end survey. However, teachers noted that scores on unit tests, which still required real understanding, did not improve or decline significantly.
options: Test scores improved significantly after the grading change.
Student anxiety increased after homework was graded for completion.
The grading change appeared to ease student anxiety without affecting test performance.
The grading change caused test scores to decline sharply.
quests.correctAnswer: The grading change appeared to ease student anxiety without affecting test performance.
quests.hint: Notice that the passage separates the effect on anxiety from the effect on test scores.
quests.explanation: Anxiety dropped after the grading change, but test scores stayed roughly the same, showing the change affected how students felt without changing how much they actually learned.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national rail service introduced a discounted off-peak fare aimed at retirees and students. Within a year, ridership during previously quiet midday hours had grown substantially, while ridership during the already-crowded morning rush hour remained essentially unchanged.
options: Rush-hour ridership grew the most after the discount was introduced.
The discount appears to have drawn new riders specifically to off-peak hours.
Ridership fell during midday hours after the discount began.
The discount had an identical effect on every time of day.
quests.correctAnswer: The discount appears to have drawn new riders specifically to off-peak hours.
quests.hint: Compare what happened to midday ridership versus rush-hour ridership.
quests.explanation: Midday ridership grew substantially while rush-hour numbers barely changed, suggesting the off-peak discount successfully targeted the time period it was designed for.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A high school athletic director required all coaches to complete a course on recognizing concussion symptoms before the season began. That season, the number of athletes removed from games due to suspected head injuries rose sharply, while the number of athletes who returned to play the same day after a hard hit fell to nearly zero.
options: Coaches became less cautious about head injuries after the training.
The training appears to have made coaches more cautious about head injuries.
The number of suspected head injuries dropped after the training.
Athletes returned to play immediately after hard hits more often than before.
quests.correctAnswer: The training appears to have made coaches more cautious about head injuries.
quests.hint: Think about what an increase in athletes being removed from games, alongside a drop in same-day returns, suggests about coaches' behavior.
quests.explanation: More athletes were removed for suspected injuries and far fewer returned the same day, suggesting coaches became more careful about identifying and responding to possible concussions after the training.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A chain of grocery stores began labeling shelf prices with a cost-per-ounce figure in addition to the total price. Store managers reported that sales of store-brand products, which were often cheaper per ounce but had higher total prices due to smaller package sizes, increased in the months that followed.
options: The added price information seems to have helped shoppers notice better value.
Sales of store-brand products fell after the new labels appeared.
The cost-per-ounce labels confused customers so much that sales dropped overall.
Package size had no relationship to how the products were priced.
quests.correctAnswer: The added price information seems to have helped shoppers notice better value.
quests.hint: Think about what the cost-per-ounce label reveals that the total price alone does not.
quests.explanation: Store-brand sales rose once shoppers could see the true cost per ounce, suggesting the added information helped them recognize a better value that wasn't obvious from the total price alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A neighborhood watch program that once relied on printed newsletters mailed quarterly switched to a group chat where residents could post updates instantly. Police records show that the average time between a resident noticing suspicious activity and reporting it to authorities dropped from several hours to under fifteen minutes.
options: Reporting times grew longer after the switch to a group chat.
Residents stopped reporting suspicious activity after the change.
The switch to instant messaging appears to have sped up how quickly residents reported concerns.
How residents communicated had no effect on reporting speed.
quests.correctAnswer: The switch to instant messaging appears to have sped up how quickly residents reported concerns.
quests.hint: Compare how long it took residents to report suspicious activity before and after the change.
quests.explanation: The average reporting time dropped drastically once residents could post instantly instead of waiting for a mailed newsletter, suggesting the faster communication method sped up reporting.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A behavioral economist studied two groups of new employees at the same company: one group's retirement contributions increased automatically by one percent every year unless they opted out, while the other group's contributions stayed fixed unless they manually increased them. Five years later, the automatic-increase group had saved substantially more on average.
options: The group with fixed contributions saved more over five years.
Automatic yearly increases appear to result in greater retirement savings than requiring manual changes.
Both groups ended up with identical savings after five years.
Whether contributions increase automatically makes no difference to long-term savings.
quests.correctAnswer: Automatic yearly increases appear to result in greater retirement savings than requiring manual changes.
quests.hint: Compare the savings outcomes of the two groups after five years.
quests.explanation: The group with automatic yearly increases saved considerably more than the group that had to manually increase contributions, suggesting the automatic default made a meaningful difference over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Engineers at an electric vehicle company noticed that cars equipped with a new battery-cooling system maintained their advertised driving range even after two years of daily use, while cars with the older cooling system showed a noticeable drop in range over the same period.
options: Cars with the new cooling system lost range faster than older models.
Battery range is unaffected by the type of cooling system used.
The new cooling system appears to help batteries maintain their range over time.
Both cooling systems produced identical results after two years.
quests.correctAnswer: The new cooling system appears to help batteries maintain their range over time.
quests.hint: Compare how driving range changed over two years for each type of cooling system.
quests.explanation: Cars with the new cooling system kept their range steady over two years, while older systems showed a decline, suggesting the new technology helps batteries age better.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since switching from a paper planner to a shared digital calendar with her husband, Priya says she has stopped double-booking herself and no longer needs to ask him what their evening plans are, since she can simply check the calendar herself.
options: The shared digital calendar seems to have reduced scheduling confusion for Priya.
Priya double-books herself more often since switching to a digital calendar.
Priya stopped using any calendar at all.
Priya's husband refuses to use the shared calendar.
quests.correctAnswer: The shared digital calendar seems to have reduced scheduling confusion for Priya.
quests.hint: Compare Priya's scheduling problems before and after switching to a shared calendar.
quests.explanation: Priya no longer double-books herself or needs to ask about plans, showing that the shared digital calendar has reduced confusion around scheduling.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A consulting firm that once required all client presentations to be delivered in person began allowing consultants to choose between in-person and video presentations. Client satisfaction scores stayed roughly the same regardless of format, but consultants reported significantly less job-related travel fatigue after the policy changed.
options: The flexible presentation policy mainly benefited consultants rather than changing client satisfaction.
Client satisfaction scores rose sharply once video presentations were allowed.
Consultants reported more travel fatigue after the policy changed.
The format of a presentation had no effect on anything measured.
quests.correctAnswer: The flexible presentation policy mainly benefited consultants rather than changing client satisfaction.
quests.hint: Notice which outcome changed after the policy shift, and which one stayed the same.
quests.explanation: Client satisfaction remained steady, but consultant fatigue dropped, suggesting the main benefit of the new policy was for the consultants rather than a change in how clients felt.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A study comparing two groups of office workers found that those given adjustable-height desks used them to stand for an average of only twenty minutes a day, far less than the two hours researchers had expected, even though most participants said in surveys that they intended to stand more.
options: Workers stood for far more time than researchers expected.
Workers never used their adjustable desks in the standing position.
Having access to a standing desk did not translate into as much standing as workers expected.
Workers' intentions matched exactly how much they actually stood.
quests.correctAnswer: Having access to a standing desk did not translate into as much standing as workers expected.
quests.hint: Compare what workers said they intended to do with what they actually did.
quests.explanation: Workers stood for far less time than they expected or intended, showing a gap between people's stated intentions and their actual behavior with the new desks.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A video game studio released a major update that added a difficulty option specifically designed for players who wanted a relaxed, story-focused experience without combat challenges. Player reviews mentioning the story improved noticeably after the update, even among players who never selected the new difficulty option.
options: The new option may have changed how all players perceived the game, not just those who used it.
Only players who used the new difficulty mode left improved reviews.
Reviews mentioning the story became more negative after the update.
The update had no effect on how players reviewed the story.
quests.correctAnswer: The new option may have changed how all players perceived the game, not just those who used it.
quests.hint: Notice that story reviews improved even among players who didn't use the new feature.
quests.explanation: Story-related reviews improved broadly, even among players who never chose the new relaxed mode, suggesting the update's presence may have shifted overall perception of the game.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Despite living three hours apart, the Okafor siblings have maintained a tradition of cooking the same recipe together over video call every Sunday since their mother passed away two years ago, each preparing their portion in their own kitchen while talking through the process together.
options: The video-call cooking tradition seems to help the siblings feel connected despite the distance.
The siblings stopped speaking after their mother passed away.
The siblings live in the same house.
The siblings have abandoned the tradition since it began.
quests.correctAnswer: The video-call cooking tradition seems to help the siblings feel connected despite the distance.
quests.hint: Think about what maintaining this weekly tradition, despite the distance, suggests about the siblings' relationship.
quests.explanation: Continuing the Sunday cooking tradition over video call for two years, despite living far apart, suggests it helps the siblings stay connected to each other and to their mother's memory.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city that switched its public bus fleet from diesel to electric engines saw measurable improvements in air quality readings near major bus routes within eighteen months, while air quality readings in neighborhoods without bus routes showed no significant change over the same period.
options: Air quality improved equally across the entire city.
The switch to electric buses appears linked to air quality improvements specifically along bus routes.
Air quality worsened near bus routes after the switch.
The type of bus engine has no connection to air quality.
quests.correctAnswer: The switch to electric buses appears linked to air quality improvements specifically along bus routes.
quests.hint: Compare the air quality changes in neighborhoods with bus routes to those without.
quests.explanation: Air quality improved near bus routes but not in areas without them, suggesting the switch to electric buses was specifically responsible for the change.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An online retailer that once displayed only a product's average star rating began also showing the total number of reviews next to it. Analysts found that products with a 4.2-star rating based on thousands of reviews began outselling products with a 4.8-star rating based on only a handful of reviews, a pattern that had not existed before the change.
options: Shoppers always preferred the highest star rating regardless of review count.
The number of reviews shown had no effect on purchasing decisions.
Products with fewer reviews always outsold products with more reviews.
Shoppers appear to trust ratings backed by more reviews, even if the rating itself is slightly lower.
quests.correctAnswer: Shoppers appear to trust ratings backed by more reviews, even if the rating itself is slightly lower.
quests.hint: Compare how sales patterns changed once the number of reviews became visible.
quests.explanation: Products with more reviews began outselling those with higher ratings but fewer reviews, suggesting that once review counts were visible, shoppers placed real trust in that number.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university replaced its traditional three-hour final exams with a series of shorter assessments spread across the semester. Students reported lower stress levels in surveys, and the percentage of students withdrawing from courses before completion dropped for the first time in five years.
options: Spreading assessments throughout the semester appears connected to lower stress and fewer withdrawals.
Course withdrawals increased after the assessment format changed.
Student stress levels rose after the change.
The format of assessments has no bearing on student stress or withdrawal rates.
quests.correctAnswer: Spreading assessments throughout the semester appears connected to lower stress and fewer withdrawals.
quests.hint: Notice the two outcomes mentioned together, and consider what they have in common.
quests.explanation: Both stress and course withdrawals decreased after the university spread out its assessments, suggesting the new format reduced the pressure that had been pushing some students to drop courses.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's annual folk festival, which had struggled with declining attendance for years, began offering free admission to anyone under eighteen while keeping adult ticket prices the same. The following year, overall attendance grew, and organizers noted that many attending families included both a paying adult and multiple children who would not have attended otherwise.
options: Waiving admission for children appears to have drawn in more family attendance overall.
Overall attendance dropped after admission became free for children.
Adult ticket prices were lowered along with children's admission.
Family attendance was unaffected by the change in admission policy.
quests.correctAnswer: Waiving admission for children appears to have drawn in more family attendance overall.
quests.hint: Think about how removing the cost barrier for children might change a family's decision to attend.
quests.explanation: Attendance grew after admission became free for children, and organizers observed more families attending together, suggesting the price change removed a barrier that had been keeping some families away.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A budget hotel chain that once left thermostats on a fixed setting installed smart thermostats controllable from guests' phones. Guest satisfaction scores related to room comfort rose only slightly, but the chain's energy costs across all properties dropped by nearly twenty percent within the first year.
options: Guest satisfaction scores rose dramatically after the thermostats were installed.
Energy costs increased after the smart thermostats were installed.
The thermostats had no measurable effect on either comfort or costs.
The smart thermostats seem to have benefited the hotel's costs more than guest comfort ratings.
quests.correctAnswer: The smart thermostats seem to have benefited the hotel's costs more than guest comfort ratings.
quests.hint: Compare the size of the change in guest satisfaction to the size of the change in energy costs.
quests.explanation: Guest comfort scores rose only slightly, while energy costs dropped substantially, suggesting the smart thermostats delivered a much bigger benefit for the hotel's costs than for how comfortable guests felt.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A public library that had been open only during standard business hours began opening two evenings a week specifically for people who work daytime jobs. Card sign-ups from adults aged twenty-five to forty-five, a group that had been underrepresented among library users, rose noticeably in the months that followed.
options: Sign-ups from working-age adults dropped after the evening hours began.
The library removed its evening hours due to low interest.
The evening hours appear to have reached working adults who couldn't visit before.
Library hours have no relationship to who signs up for a card.
quests.correctAnswer: The evening hours appear to have reached working adults who couldn't visit before.
quests.hint: Think about which group of people would benefit most from evening hours.
quests.explanation: Sign-ups from working-age adults rose after evening hours were added, suggesting the new schedule reached people who couldn't visit during standard business hours.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A smart home company found that customers who set up their devices with the help of an in-app guided walkthrough contacted customer support 70 percent less often in their first month than customers who set up devices without using the walkthrough.
options: Customers who used the walkthrough contacted support more often.
The walkthrough had no measurable effect on support contact rates.
Every customer contacted support the same number of times.
The guided walkthrough appears to reduce the need for customer support.
quests.correctAnswer: The guided walkthrough appears to reduce the need for customer support.
quests.hint: Compare support contact rates between customers who used the walkthrough and those who didn't.
quests.explanation: Customers who used the guided walkthrough contacted support far less often, suggesting the walkthrough helped them resolve setup issues on their own.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional running club that had always scheduled its weekly group runs for early Saturday morning added a second option on Wednesday evenings after several members mentioned scheduling conflicts. Membership renewals for the following year reached their highest level in the club's history.
options: Membership renewals dropped to their lowest level after the change.
Adding a second run time may have addressed scheduling conflicts that were affecting renewals.
The club removed the Saturday morning run entirely.
When runs are scheduled has no bearing on membership renewals.
quests.correctAnswer: Adding a second run time may have addressed scheduling conflicts that were affecting renewals.
quests.hint: Think about what problem members had mentioned before the schedule change.
quests.explanation: Renewals reached a record high after a second run time was added to address scheduling conflicts members had raised, suggesting the change resolved a real barrier to staying in the club.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A restaurant chain tested removing calorie counts from its menu in half of its locations while keeping them visible in the other half, as a temporary experiment. Average order size and total spending per customer were nearly identical between the two groups of locations.
options: Customers ordered significantly more food when calorie counts were hidden.
Customers ordered significantly less food when calorie counts were visible.
Calorie counts caused customers to stop ordering at those locations entirely.
Displaying calorie counts did not appear to significantly change customer ordering behavior.
quests.correctAnswer: Displaying calorie counts did not appear to significantly change customer ordering behavior.
quests.hint: Compare ordering behavior between the two groups of locations.
quests.explanation: Order size and spending were nearly the same whether or not calorie counts were shown, suggesting that displaying them had little real effect on how customers ordered.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's public transit authority raised fares by fifteen percent to cover rising costs, expecting a small drop in ridership. Instead, ridership fell by nearly twenty-five percent in the following six months, and overall fare revenue ended up lower than before the increase.
options: Ridership grew after the fare increase.
The fare increase appears to have backfired by driving away more riders than expected.
Total fare revenue increased as planned after the fare hike.
The fare increase had exactly the effect the transit authority expected.
quests.correctAnswer: The fare increase appears to have backfired by driving away more riders than expected.
quests.hint: Compare what the transit authority expected with what actually happened to ridership and revenue.
quests.explanation: Ridership dropped far more than expected and revenue actually fell, suggesting the fare increase discouraged more riders than the transit authority had anticipated.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since he began leaving his phone in another room while working on his research paper, Diego says he finishes his daily writing goal in about ninety minutes, compared to the nearly three hours it used to take him when his phone stayed on the desk beside him.
options: Diego takes longer to write since moving his phone to another room.
Diego stopped setting any writing goals for himself.
Where Diego keeps his phone has no effect on his writing speed.
Keeping his phone away from his desk seems to have made Diego's writing more efficient.
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping his phone away from his desk seems to have made Diego's writing more efficient.
quests.hint: Compare how long Diego's writing sessions took before and after he started leaving his phone elsewhere.
quests.explanation: Diego's writing time dropped from nearly three hours to about ninety minutes once he moved his phone out of reach, suggesting the change helped him focus and work more efficiently.
